dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether _tombstone_folding_commit should pick the earliest (original) addition (e.g. `--reverse` + first, or commits[-1]) rather than the most-recent commits[0].
evidence: src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:130-131: commits = [line.strip() for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]  /  return commits[0] if commits else None
git log defaults to reverse-chronological order (newest first); commits[0] is thus the latest addition, not the earliest folding commit
src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:22-25: docstring: 'it inspects the local remote-tracking tickets ref for the configured sync remote'
src/rebar/_store/reclaim_eligibility.py:118-124: run_git(root, "log", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=%H", "--", path, ...) — no start revision, so git log defaults to HEAD
ABSENCE: no rev argument scoping the log to refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
dropped.finding: _tombstone_folding_commit takes commits[0] from `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H` which is reverse-chronological, so it selects the MOST-RECENT commit that added the path, not the original folding commit. If a `.retired` tombstone path was ever removed and re-added, this identifies the wrong folding commit and can mis-anchor the horizon (making a long-standing tombstone look recently added, i.e. ineligible).
merged_from: _tombstone_folding_commit runs `git log ... -- path` with no explicit revision, so it discovers the folding commit from the current HEAD/checked-out branch rather than the configured remote-tracking tickets ref the module docstring emphasizes ('inspects the local remote-tracking tickets ref'). The reachability check downstream mitigates correctness, but the discovery scope is inconsistent with the stated read-only-remote contract and can miss the intended commit if HEAD is not the tickets branch.
scenarios: A tombstone path that was created, deleted, then re-created in later history
dropped.suggested_fix: Select the earliest addition: use `git log --reverse --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- <path>` and take commits[0], or take commits[-1] from the default ordering.
